io_reference.note: output hold needs data >= L_ref_min + hold_skew 50 + unc 25 at FF

route_ff_before_eco.eco: hold ECO hm 30: 1,543 endpoints below 30 ps padded (2,137 cells)

cause: Clock-spine topology skew after routing, not late rs_o leaves. The count-bisection spine (node = count-weighted centroid) pulls its trunk toward the dense W band (rsp_data_p 133 leaves + rd2/rd3 126 leaves); the E rs_o launch leaves (rsd_o, x 245-249) hang on a long wire-dominated branch and were balanced at placement by pad chains on the W leaves (W 3-4 pads, E 0-1). After routing the wire-dominated E branch is faster than estimated: E rsd_o sinks arrive 351-377 ps (mean 370) TT, the W pin-flop band (the IO reference) 394-419 (mean 407), N/S g_s1b 380. The output hold requirement is keyed to the W reference band, so every output paid ~37 ps TT of extra data delay: in-flow hold repair BUFx2 (19-28 ps TT) then the routed hold ECO (hm 30) 2x HB2 (30-54 ps TT mean); rs_o carries 2-4 hold cells, mean 72.6 ps TT (max 107.6). Without those cells the worst output launch is 158.5 ps.
fix: Symmetric insertion-aware spine (OT_SPINE_SYM=1: nodes at the bounding-box centre of their leaves, so the E and W branches see the same span; OT_SPINE_TREE_PAD=1: residual pads in the tree, not at the leaves; OT_SPINE_SAFE_BALANCE=1), same root port ck at N centre, same pins, RTL, outline, pads and cycles. Expect boundary leaves (W reference band vs E/N/S output flops) within the spread budget after routing, so the kit HB2 output stage meets FF without in-flow/route hold chains.
